summary: Decoupled Phase 2 objectives to eliminate Pareto collapse (objective_corr_f1_f3≈1.00) and made robust return the default f3 signal for OOS-focused mode.

changes.config.py: Changed PHASE2_USE_TOTAL_RETURN_OBJ default from False to True so f3 uses robust return (min train/val) instead of profit_factor. Updated comments.
changes.phase2_rule_pool.py: In compute_phase2_objectives_from_metrics: (1) Removed trade_penalty from f1 and f3 (kept on f2 only). (2) Removed overfit_gap_penalty from f1 (kept on f3 only). Updated module docstring. Previously all three objectives received identical trade_penalty and f1/f3 both received overfit_gap_penalty, causing Pareto collapse.
changes.test_phase2_rule_pool.py: Updated overfit_gap_penalty tests to assert on f3 instead of f1. Updated trade_penalty test to expect f3=0 (no trade_penalty). Added 4 new tests: test_penalties_not_identical_across_objectives, test_trade_penalty_only_on_f2, test_f3_uses_robust_return_by_default, test_pf_floor_still_penalizes_support.
changes.test_evox_runner.py: Updated test_low_trade_drawdown_penalty to reflect trade_penalty only on f2.

notes: PF floor and feasibility gates remain intact (PHASE2_PROFIT_FACTOR_FLOOR still adds to support_penalty, which affects all objectives via weighted penalty terms).
Diversity penalty is retained on f1 and f3 (consistent with original design).
Support penalty weights (F1=0.4, F2=0.6, F3=0.6) differentiate the shared penalty across objectives.
The trade_penalty (PHASE2_INFEASIBLE_OBJECTIVE_PENALTY=50) now only affects f2 (drawdown objective), which naturally relates to trade count.
overfit_gap_penalty is now f3-only (robust-return objective), which aligns with the return-based nature of the penalty.
risks: Changing PHASE2_USE_TOTAL_RETURN_OBJ default from False to True changes the f3 signal from profit_factor to robust return. Any code path that relied on the old default (f3=profit_factor) without explicitly setting the config will now see different f3 values.

Removing trade_penalty from f1 and f3 means low-trade-count rules will have much better f1 and f3 scores (though they still get dd_for_obj=100 on f2). This could increase feasible-looking-but-untradeable rules on the Pareto front.
The overfit_gap_penalty was on f1 for a reason (Sortino can also overfit). Moving it to f3-only means Sortino-based overfitting is no longer directly penalized.
